## From SSD storage to R memory

**SSD:** `data/seedlings.csv`

```{.r}
seedlings <- read.csv("data/seedlings.csv")
```

**R memory (RAM):** `seedlings` — the table read from the CSV.

The CSV stays unchanged on the SSD.

::: notes
0–3 minutes, including title. Trace SSD file -> read.csv -> data frame in RAM.
The assignment retains the returned data frame under the name seedlings.
After restarting R with workspace restore disabled, run the import again.
In browser RStudio, storage and R memory are on the server: upload the file first.
:::

:::

::: notes
3–6 minutes. Show day3-2/project/ in the repository. The separate participant ZIP
names this folder AFEC-R-basics/ when extracted; its contents are the same.
Reveal extensions in the file manager
if hidden. Folder names are conventions, not special R syntax. Changing a file
extension alone does not convert its contents. Keep data unchanged and save
instructions separately. Quarto uses Markdown for the prose; no syntax lesson.
:::

## Absolute and relative paths

| Path | Example | R's working directory |
|---|---|---|
| Absolute · Windows | `C:/work/data/seedlings.csv` | Anywhere |
| Absolute · macOS | `/Users/alex/data/seedlings.csv` | Anywhere |
| Absolute · Linux | `/home/alex/data/seedlings.csv` | Anywhere |
| Relative · All three | `data/seedlings.csv` | Project folder here |

**For sharing:** open the Project and use relative paths.

::: notes
6–12 minutes. Absolute examples are illustrative, not paths to copy.
Absolute paths give the full location from the drive/filesystem root and work
from any working directory if that file exists. Relative paths start from R's
current working directory; the next slide sets it by opening the Project.
Personal absolute paths usually need editing on another computer.
macOS absolute paths also start with /. Use forward slashes in quoted R paths.
Relative paths still need a known starting point; introduce the Project next.
Show how the absolute path changes when the project moves, while data/seedlings.csv stays the same.
In browser RStudio, paths refer to the server's filesystem.
:::

## Open the Project, then use relative paths

Open `day3-2/project/AFEC-R-basics.Rproj`,
then `R/inspect_seedlings.R`.

```{.r}
seedlings <- read.csv("data/seedlings.csv")
```

R looks for `data/` inside the **Project folder**, even when the code is in `R/`.

::: notes
12–19 minutes. Briefly demonstrate opening the prepared Project and script.
Use Project-relative paths without getwd()/setwd() commands in the lesson.
Avoid setwd() with a personal absolute path: another computer may lack that path.
Relative paths alone do not guarantee reproducibility: preserve the starting
context and folder structure. Opening a script alone does not set that context.
If input is missing, reopen the correct Project and check folder names.
Source: https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/code/projects.html
:::

## Saving code and running code

```{.r}
diameter <- c(2.1, 3.4, 4.7)
diameter
```

| Action | What changes? |
|---|---|
| Save the script | Code saved on the computer |
| Run `diameter <- ...` | Values stored in R as `diameter` |
| Run `diameter` | Values shown in the Console |

After restarting R, run the script again.

::: notes
19–22 minutes. Show what changes after Save and after Run, following the code together.
Do not repeat the Harry/Potter arithmetic drills. If time permits restart R and
rerun the two lines; otherwise describe this and do one restart in the practical.
The supplied Project disables workspace restore/save. A Project alone does not
save data objects or guarantee reproducibility. Saving a script also does not
save its most recent printed results.
:::

## Reading a CSV creates an object

```{.r}
seedlings <- read.csv("data/seedlings.csv")
```

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"data/seedlings.csv"` | Input file |
| `read.csv(...)` | Read the CSV as a table |
| `seedlings <-` | Store it as `seedlings` |



::: notes
22–25 minutes. The in-memory object supports inspection and plotting; editing
it does not rewrite the CSV. Distinguish the quotes from the unquoted object name and case.
Explain right side evaluated before assignment. Reading again refreshes the
object from disk; running a later plotting line does not automatically reread a
changed CSV. CSV is one supported format, not the only format R can read.
Source: R read.table/read.csv documentation.
:::

## Values and tables

::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
### Values

- **Numeric (numbers):** `2.1`, `3.4`.
- **Character (text):** `"Species_A"`.
- **Logical (true/false):** `TRUE`, `FALSE`.

`NA`: missing value.
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
### How values are stored

- **Vector:** values of the same type in order.
- **Data frame:** a table.

All columns have the same number of rows.
:::
:::



::: notes
25–29 minutes. Restrict vector here to ordinary atomic vectors, each with one
underlying type. A general list can mix object types; a data frame is a list of
columns with equal row counts. This one sentence is enough; no list exercise.
In R numeric usually means double here. If asked, 30 is numeric/double whereas
30L is integer; storage type does not determine a variable's scientific role.
NA is an indicator, not a separate ordinary measurement type.
:::

## Rows and columns

```{r preview}
head(seedlings, 3)
```

**One row = one seedling**, measured and checked later for survival.

```{r structure}
str(seedlings)
```

::: notes
29–33 minutes. The data are fictional, not a subset of Day 1–3's model data.
Species_A/Species_B are fictional labels. Read 8 observations, 4 variables, chr,
num and logi aloud. Several rows can have the same species. These are seedling
stem diameters in mm, not adult DBH. The preview deliberately requests 3 rows;
head(seedlings) without that argument shows six by default.
:::

## A column is a vector

```{r column}
diameter <- seedlings$diameter_mm
class(seedlings)
class(diameter)
length(diameter)
```

`$diameter_mm`: the diameter column, one value per seedling.

```{r mixed-vector}
class(c(2.1, "unmeasured"))
```

Numbers mixed with text → all values become text.

::: notes
33–37 minutes. class identifies an object's class, not a complete specification
of its internal storage; no typeof detour. Show that "unmeasured" in an otherwise
numeric CSV column may change its imported class too. Keep numeric measurement
and missingness separate. This is one demonstration of coercion, not a type
conversion tutorial. The assignment copies values semantically; it creates no
live link that writes back to the data frame or input file.
:::

## Missing is different from zero or death

```{r missing}
is.na(diameter)
seedlings$survived
```

- Diameter `NA`: unmeasured, not zero.
- Survival `FALSE`: observed dead.
- Survival `NA`: unknown.

`is.na()`: `TRUE` for missing entries.

::: notes
37–41 minutes. Missing diameter is record 4; missing survival is record 5.
The input token NA becomes a missing marker with this import function. The text
"NA" in an R character vector is distinct from R's missing marker. Do not
substitute 0 or FALSE for unknown values or introduce imputation here.
Source: https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/NA.html
:::

## Looking at the data

| Code | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `class(seedlings)` | What kind of object it is |
| `str(seedlings)` | Column types and a few values |
| `head(seedlings)` | First six rows |
| `dim(seedlings)` | Number of rows, then columns |



::: notes
41–45 minutes. head previews rows without removing the remaining observations.
str reveals the column type; class of the whole table alone does
not. Read the output together: a numeric-looking printed value alone does not
establish its type. Scientific interpretation also needs the data dictionary
and units. Do not reteach names, levels, summary and tail as a second catalogue.
:::

## Make a report with Quarto

`report.qmd`: text + R code → **Render** → `report.html`

The code in the QMD reads the CSV. The HTML shows the report.

Open `report.qmd` → click **Render** → open `report.html`.

::: notes
55–58 minutes. This is required: read the text and R code in report.qmd
alongside the class, click Render and show the resulting HTML. Use the prepared
RStudio environment with Quarto and knitr available; no classroom installation.
The report reads its own CSV, independently of Console objects. Its QMD is at
the participant Project root, so the default document-directory execution finds
data/. If rendering fails, show the prepared HTML and explain the same steps;
record the environment problem for follow-up. Do not omit the Quarto explanation.
Source: https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html
:::
